scenario: Two acquaintances run into each other at Target, one of them volunteers there (a special event) and is in charge of giving away free samples
learner_goal: Give away free samples (<extra_info>Extra information: your manager has told you to clear out the samples before your shift ends.</extra_info>)
partner_goal: Try to get as many free samples as possible without appearing too greedy (<extra_info>Extra information: you love free stuff but you also don't want the person to think you're taking advantage of the situation</extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Oliver Thompson
transcript.content: Hey Ethan — fancy seeing you here! I'm running the sample table today and my manager wants these cleared out before my shift ends. Want to try one? Help yourself — take as many as you like.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Smith
transcript.content: Thanks, Oliver — you're a lifesaver. Mind if I grab a few to try and share with some neighbors? Three or four should be perfect. Which one would you recommend I try first?

transcript.speaker: Oliver Thompson
transcript.content: Perfect — go ahead and grab three or four. If I had to pick one to try first, I'd recommend the lemon-ginger; it's bright and usually a crowd-pleaser. Want me to put together a little mixed pack for you to share?

transcript.speaker: Ethan Smith
transcript.content: Yes please — a mixed pack sounds perfect. If there are any extras, could I grab a couple more lemon-ginger? I’ll share them with some neighbors. Thanks, Oliver — I really appreciate it.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Thompson
transcript.content: Absolutely — I’ll put together a mixed pack and slip in two extra lemon-ginger for you. I’ll bag them up now; they’ll be ready in a minute. Glad you’re sharing them with the neighbors.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Smith
transcript.content: Awesome — thanks so much, Oliver. I really appreciate it. I’ll grab the mixed pack when it’s ready. If there’s anything else you need to clear out before your shift ends, I’m happy to take extras off your hands and share them with a few neighbors.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Thompson
transcript.content: Perfect — I’ll bag up the mixed pack with the two extra lemon-ginger and set it on the counter for you. If you want more to share, I’ve got a few mango and green-tea samples I can add; otherwise this should be plenty. I’ll bring it over in a minute — good to see you, Ethan.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Smith
transcript.content: Perfect — thanks so much, Oliver. If you don’t mind, could you also slip in two mango and one green‑tea? I’ll swing by the counter in a minute to grab the bag. And if there’s anything left at the end of your shift, I’m happy to take extras off your hands to share with the neighbors.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Thompson
transcript.content: Got it — I’ll tuck two mango and one green‑tea into your mixed pack and set the bag on the counter. Swing by in a minute and I’ll hand it to you. Nice running into you, Ethan.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Smith
transcript.content: Thanks so much, Oliver — I’ll swing by in a minute to grab it. If anything’s left over at the end of your shift, would you mind slipping me a couple more lemon‑ginger? I’ll share them with a few neighbors on Maple. Really appreciate it — good luck with the rest of your shift!
